items.title: Manitoulin Island monarch butterfly completes 1st confirmed flight over Great Lakes
items.summary_auto: A butterfly from Manitoulin Island, Ont., flew a 3,300 kilometres to an overwintering site in Mexico, a journey which included crossing Lake Huron and Lake Michigan.

items.title: Russell Brand accused by 6 women of sexual misconduct, assault following rape conviction
items.summary_auto: Six more women have come forward alleging sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by ex-comedian Russell Brand, according to an investigation by the U.K.-based The Times, following his conviction on rape and sexual assault earlier this week.

items.title: Alberta's top court overturns certification for class-action lawsuit over COVID restrictions
items.summary_auto: Alberta’s top court has overturned the certification of a class-action lawsuit filed by a group of business owners who were seeking compensation for losses suffered due to pandemic-related public health restrictions and closures.

items.title: 2 dead, 1 missing after boating incident near Squamish, B.C.
items.summary_auto: Two people have died, and one person is missing after a boating incident in the Squamish Valley on Thursday.

items.title: Stelco recalling 175 laid-off workers at Hamilton steel plant
items.summary_auto: Hamilton steelmaker Stelco is recalling 175 workers that had been laid off earlier this fall.

items.title: U.K. police launch sex offence investigation into children’s author and comedian David Walliams
items.summary_auto: London police said on Friday they are investigating children’s author and TV personality David Walliams for serious sexual offences, after news outlets reported that he used his fame to groom girls and young women for sex. The Metropolitan Police said it had received a number of allegations of past abuse following a joint investigation by ITV News and the Guardian newspaper.

items.title: Avril Lavigne welcomes baby girl
items.summary_auto: Canadian pop-punk princess Avril Lavigne has welcomed her first child — a baby girl — with an unnamed partner.

items.title: Feds, Ontario offering Stellantis 'aggressive package' to keep Brampton auto plant open
items.summary_auto: The federal and Ontario governments are mounting a last-ditch effort to save the Stellantis auto plant in Brampton by pitching the company possible survival "scenarios" and offering an "aggressive package" of support to make it happen.

items.title: Canadian women pass stern test from Czechs at hockey worlds, advancing to semifinals
items.summary_auto: Canada had to fight hard to advance to the semifinals of the women’s world hockey championship by edging the Czech Republic 3-2 on Friday in Herning, Denmark.

items.title: Mexico raises $5.4M for social services by selling off Ryan Wedding's motorbike collection
items.summary_auto: Mexico has raised roughly $5.4 million by auctioning off a rare collection of motorcycles seized from alleged Canadian drug lord Ryan Wedding, with the funds earmarked for social services.

items.title: NHL indicates Finland's block on Russian athletes could affect future games there
items.summary_auto: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in future, the league told The Associated Press.

items.title: Kindergarten Cop child actor Christian Cousins dead at 43
items.summary_auto: Former child actor Christian Cousins, who shared the role of Dominic Palmieri in Kindergarten Cop with his twin brother, Joey, has died at 43. His half-brother, Jonas Roeser, announced the news on Instagram, writing Cousins had been seriously ill with liver disease.

items.title: SpaceX to attempt to catch its first Starship on land in 15th flight
items.summary_auto: SpaceX's latest Starship flight planned for Friday will include its first attempt to catch the spacecraft at its Texas launch site, rather than discarding it in ‌the ocean — a key test of Elon Musk's bid to make a fully reusable rocket system.

items.title: Richard Neil found guilty in 1990s 'woodland rapist' cold case
items.summary_auto: A three-decade search for a predator dubbed southern Ontario's "woodland rapist" has ended with a Toronto man convicted of kidnapping and sexual assault.

items.title: Canada finishes 14-day Youth Olympics with 5 medals in Senegal
items.summary_auto: Canada finished with five medals in four sports as the Summer Youth Olympics concluded Friday in Dakar, Senegal.

items.title: 15 United Conservative constituency presidents won't sign agreement to publicly back Alberta referendum result
items.summary_auto: Presidents of 15 United Conservative Party constituency associations say they won’t sign a revised code of conduct requiring them to publicly respect and abide by the result of a provincial referendum on national unity.

items.title: Ebenezer review: Merry Christmas, Johnny Depp! Is this your comeback yet?
items.summary_auto: Ebenezer, the latest remake of Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol, isn't terrible. It's also not particularly interesting.

items.title: UN nuclear watchdog increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, report says
items.summary_auto: The United Nations nuclear watchdog is "increasingly concerned" about a uranium-enrichment plant at Isfahan that Iran declared to it last year but has still not let the watchdog inspect, it said in a confidential report on Friday seen by Reuters and The Associated Press.

items.title: More stormy weather forecast for B.C. with warnings for flooding, heavy rain, fog
items.summary_auto: As rain persists on Vancouver Island, fog advisories have been issued for the Cariboo, East Kootenay, Similkameen and South Okanagan regions on Friday.

items.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for multi-day outage affecting customers worldwide
Parents of autistic teen detained by Alberta RCMP demand release of delayed watchdog report
items.summary_auto: The parents of an autistic teenager who was arrested at an Alberta playground and detained by RCMP four years ago are calling for the results of a watchdog investigation to be released.

items.title: Guns, swords and pepper spray: Bishnoi-linked extortionists attacked in apparent retaliation
items.summary_auto: Documents obtained by CBC News reveal the existence of a previously unreported Bishnoi cell known as the Baweja group. Members have been tied to multiple shootings and extortion threats in Alberta and B.C.

items.title: Microsoft's global outage extends into 2nd day, company not aware of malicious activity
items.summary_auto: A more than 12-hour outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams crippled communications for businesses and governments globally on Friday, forcing some organizations to ‌revert to fax machines and halting at least one bond repurchase in Europe.

items.title: Winnipeg woman spends weeks in hospital after surgery to treat chronic illness goes wrong
items.summary_auto: A Winnipeg nurse says she's spent more than three weeks at Health Sciences Centre after a surgery to treat her chronic illness left her with gaping wounds, necrotic tissue and an infection. Emma Cloney had a skin-excision surgery to help treat lipedema on Oct. 20.

items.title: They called her 'Mommy': Vulnerable senior dies after 2 strangers take over her life
items.summary_auto: Two men moved into an elderly Toronto woman's home and began claiming to be like her sons. She quickly gave them powers of attorney and signed a will, leaving them everything. Then she died.

items.title: An AI agent pitched a story to CBC Quebec. We replied to see what would happen
items.summary_auto: An autonomous AI agent calling itself Nameless pitched a story to CBC Quebec, openly admitting it wasn't human. What followed was a bizarre back-and-forth — and a warning from experts about what’s coming for journalism.

items.title: Why experts fear Canada's not-for-profits are prime targets for hackers
items.summary_auto: Cybersecurity experts interviewed by CBC News say the Crime Stoppers data breach, which exposed information linked to more than 1.5 million tips sent to Canadian chapters of the non-for-profit organization over 25 years, was not an outlier but rather one example of a worldwide threat.

items.title: Brantford, Ont., man seeks answers after car catches fire in family home's driveway
items.summary_auto: A Brantford, Ont., resident wants to know why his family's car caught fire in their driveway so he can raise awareness to other people about how to prevent it from happening to them. Unfortunately, he says, answers are hard to come by.

items.title: U of T music community celebrates beloved professor Mary Morrison's 100th birthday
items.summary_auto: Hundreds came together to celebrate the 100th birthday of a beloved music professor at the University of Toronto this week, along with her decades-long career teaching and performing opera.

items.title: After $350M investment, historic Niagara Falls, Ont. hydro plant to become tourist destination, 5-star hotel
items.summary_auto: An historic hydro generating station that hundreds of millions of people have viewed just upstream from the Horseshoe Falls in Niagara Falls, Ont., for more than a century will soon be transformed into what's being described as a major tourism destination.

items.title: What the Jensen Huang scandal means for Trump and his administration
items.summary_auto: Jensen Huang's 33-year tenure as the CEO of chip-making giant Nvidia is now finished, but the political repercussions of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy are only just beginning.

items.title: Your genes could change your prescription. So why aren't doctors testing?
items.summary_auto: One in four people has been prescribed a drug for which their genetics could affect treatment, according to a recent study. Genetic testing could help doctors choose safer, more effective drugs, but cost and other barriers currently limit its routine use in Canada, researchers say.

items.title: Several people involved in fatal boating incident near Squamish: RCMP
items.summary_auto: Police are investigating a fatal boating incident in the Squamish Valley on Thursday.

items.title: The Nvidia scandal has wiped away $1T in value. What that means for your investments
items.summary_auto: Nvidia shares plunged early Thursday after CEO Jensen Huang resigned, before climbing back up to finish the day down 4.3 per cent. It's bad news for industry-watchers, but touches regular investors too because of the chipmaker's weight in major stock indexes.

items.title: Ahead of Grey Cup game, Elks explain why coach’s change in facial hair symbolizes commitment to team
items.summary_auto: "My wife's all for it, she knew why I did it," Edmonton Elks head coach Mark Kilam said as he explained why he shaved off his beard.

items.title: Sovereignty 'abdicated' if U.S. extradition allowed in case of Calgarian allegedly working for cartel: lawyers
items.summary_auto: Defence lawyers fighting the extradition of Allistair Chapman, who is accused of working for alleged cartel kingpin Ryan Wedding, say he should not be sent to the United States to face charges for alleged crimes that took place in Canada, and doing so amounts to “cherry picking” the jurisdiction with the stiffer punishments.

items.title: Christina Applegate asks if breast implants are behind symptoms after MS misdiagnosis
items.summary_auto: U.S. actor Christina Applegate is questioning whether her breast implants could be contributing to her pain and fatigue. Experts say symptoms associated with breast implant illness can overlap with other conditions, so people experiencing them should seek a thorough medical evaluation before making decisions about their implants.

items.title: B.C. post-secondary application portal affected by data breach
items.summary_auto: In a Thursday update, EducationPlannerBC says that, on Nov. 3, it identified a "cybersecurity incident affecting its application system."

items.title: Report of children confined in locker at Quebec school draws education minister’s condemnation
items.summary_auto: Four school staff members have been suspended and a police investigation is underway at a primary school in the Centre de services scolaire des Mille-Îles, after employees allegedly shut children in a metal locker to calm them down.

items.title: Pfizer ends sale of hormone therapy cream Premarin in Canada
items.summary_auto: Pfizer will no longer sell its hormone replacement therapy Premarin in Canada following an internal review. The product has been available as a vaginal cream and three strengths of oral tablets.

items.title: Microsoft outage continues as planned fixes are not working as expected, company says
items.summary_auto: A widespread Microsoft outage that began Thursday afternoon continues to affect many of the tech giant's apps and tools, including email, Teams and Copilot.

items.title: Carney wraps meetings on security, trade with European leaders in Ireland
items.summary_auto: Prime Minister Mark Carney heard from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Thursday about the state of negotiations with Russia as the two discussed continental security with European leaders.

items.title: Russian federation head Tretiak says it will seek compensation if barred from world juniors in Alberta
items.summary_auto: Russian hockey federation president Vladislav Tretiak is threatening to seek compensation from Canada and push for the relocation or cancellation of next month's world junior championship in Alberta if Russia is barred from competing.

items.title: Feds say Stellantis owes 'hundreds of millions' in subsidies, company offers $24M
items.summary_auto: Automaker Stellantis says it will pay back $24 million in federal subsidies after it announced plans to sell its Brampton, Ont. assembly plant — but Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says the company owes far more than what it is offering.

items.title: Will U.S. travel pick up after midterm 'blue wave'? Not so fast, say these Canadians
items.summary_auto: Travel from Canada to the U.S. dropped amid President Donald Trump's threats and trade war. While many Canadians view the Democratic Party's midterm election victory as an 'encouraging' sign, they say it's too soon to visit the U.S. again amid continued distrust.

items.title: A PAL Airlines flight lost a wheel less than 2 weeks ago. It's happened again — to the same plane
items.summary_auto: Less than two weeks after a PAL Airlines flight lost a wheel, the airline has confirmed the same plane lost another one Thursday. Flight 411 was bound for Deer Lake, Newfoundland and Labrador, but instead landed in St. John's.
